question: How do we check whether a shuttle has the right speed?

answer.reasoning: The question has one part: the sources do not say how to check whether a shuttle has the right speed. The Laws answer this directly: Law 3.1 sentences (1) and (2) describe the test stroke (full underhand stroke, contact over the back boundary line, hit at an upward angle parallel to the side lines), and Law 3.2 sentence (1) gives the pass criterion (landing not less than 530 mm and not more than 990 mm short of the other back boundary line, as in Diagram B). The ITTO clauses about who tests, how to assess the hit, and the Referee re-checking speed during play bear on the question without answering the 'how to check' part, so they go in related_sentences.
answer.answer: To test a shuttle, a player shall use a full underhand stroke which makes contact with the shuttle over the back boundary line [1]. The shuttle shall be hit at an upward angle and in a direction parallel to the side lines [2]. A shuttle of correct speed will land not less than 530 mm and not more than 990 mm short of the other back boundary line [3]. When assessing the result of the shuttle test, take into account the manner in which the shuttles were hit, including strength of shot and trajectory, and whether they were hit from the correct location over the back line [4]. The Referee shall at all times, when observing play, consider whether the shuttle speed selected before play started still appears to be correct [5].
